name: pretty-bytes
oneLiner: Turns a byte count into a short human-readable size string such as '1.34 kB'.
problem: Raw byte counts like 1337 or 1073741824 are hard to read; people want '1.34 kB' or '1 GiB'.

capabilities.name: Format a byte count
capabilities.behavior: Chooses the largest decimal unit (B, kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB, YB; base 1000) that keeps the value at or above 1, and rounds to 3 significant digits (more when the integer part already has more digits), dropping trailing zeros. A space separates number and unit.
capabilities.inputs: A finite number (or bigint) of bytes.
edgeCases: Values under 1 kB stay in bytes: 999 is '999 B'.
Rounding can promote the unit: 999999 bytes is '1 MB'.
Zero is '0 B'; -0 is treated as 0.

capabilities.name: Binary and bit unit systems
capabilities.behavior: Option 'binary' switches to base-1024 IEC units (B, KiB, MiB, GiB, ...). Option 'bits' formats the value as bits with units b, kbit, Mbit, Gbit, ... Both can be combined (kibit, Mibit, ...).
capabilities.inputs: A number plus { binary?: boolean, bits?: boolean }.
capabilities.outputs: A string in the chosen unit system.
edgeCases: The input is not multiplied by 8 in bits mode; it is already a bit count.

capabilities.name: Presentation options
capabilities.behavior: Option 'signed' prefixes '+' for positive values and a space for exactly zero (useful for diffs). Option 'space: false' removes the separator. Option 'fixedWidth' left-pads the result with spaces to a minimum length. Fraction digit options truncate (not round) to the requested number of decimals.
edgeCases: fixedWidth must be a non-negative integer, otherwise TypeError.

designIdeas: Three significant digits is the readable default.
Explicit unit systems (SI bytes, IEC bytes, bits) selected by flags rather than separate functions.
Signed output for showing size differences.
limitations: Format only: it cannot parse '1.34 kB' back into bytes.
No notion of time, so it cannot describe transfer rates.
